citeAs: Muennighoff, N., Tazi, N., Magne, L., Reimers, N. (2023). MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. EACL 2023.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers (Hugging Face, cohere.ai)
description: STS22 is a crosslingual semantic textual similarity dataset included in MTEB. It contains sentence pairs across 18 language pairs (including Arabic, English, French, German, Turkish, Spanish, Polish, Italian, Russian, and Chinese), where the goal is to assess the similarity of two sentences in different languages. Labels are continuous scores between 0 and 5, and the main metric is Spearman correlation based on cosine similarity.
inLanguage: ar, en, fr, de, tr, es, pl, it, ru, zh
name: STS22 (Crosslingual STS)
rai:dataCollection: STS22 is an existing STS benchmark dataset incorporated into MTEB. It contains crosslingual sentence pairs with similarity scores from 0 to 5. The dataset covers 18 language pairs among Arabic, English, French, German, Turkish, Spanish, Polish, Italian, Russian, and Chinese. The selection of sentences includes text from image captions, news headlines, and user forums.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentence pairs drawn from image captions, news headlines, and user forums across multiple languages.
rai:dataLimitations: MTEB notes that STS is known to poorly correlate with other real-world use cases. The benchmark also notes that very long documents are missing, and that multilingual retrieval and clustering datasets are absent, limiting comprehensive multilingual benchmarking.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports development of multilingual text embedding models, which can power a variety of applications including search systems, clustering, and text mining across multiple languages. Improved crosslingual embeddings can help bridge language barriers in NLP applications.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating text embedding models on crosslingual semantic textual similarity tasks; benchmarking multilingual embedding models; assessing the similarity of sentence pairs across different languages.
